name: Amsterdam
tagline: Gabled canal houses, Golden Age art and bikes on every bridge
description:
Amsterdam packs the charm of a much smaller town into a city of world-class museums and restless creativity. Its crescent of 17th-century canals, lined with tilting gabled merchants' houses and houseboats spilling geraniums, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, yet it feels thoroughly lived-in: bikes rattle over humpback bridges, neighbors chat on their stoops and brown cafés glow amber long after dark.

Culture comes in concentrated doses. Rembrandt and Vermeer hold court at the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh's swirling canvases fill a museum of their own, and the Anne Frank House offers one of the most moving hours you'll spend anywhere. Beyond the center lie the market bustle of De Pijp, the indie galleries of the Jordaan and the post-industrial playground of Amsterdam-Noord, a free ferry ride away.

Rent a bike, but watch and learn before joining the rush-hour stream. Snack on herring and fries with mayo, sip jenever in a centuries-old tasting room and accept that it will probably rain; the city looks its moodiest and loveliest when a gray sky is mirrored in the canals.

safety.notes: Amsterdam is very safe overall; the main hazards are pickpockets around Centraal Station and Dam Square and absent-mindedly stepping into a bike lane. Never buy drugs from street dealers, as what they sell is often a dangerous fake.

tipping: Service is included, but rounding up or adding 5–10% for good table service is appreciated.
gettingAround: Walking and cycling are the fastest ways around the compact center, and trams, buses and the metro all accept contactless cards and phones. Free ferries behind Centraal Station shuttle across the IJ to Amsterdam-Noord around the clock.
tips: Tap in and out with the same contactless card on trams, buses and the metro; forgetting to tap out charges you a hefty maximum fare.
Anne Frank House tickets are sold only online, released six weeks ahead and usually gone within hours, so set a reminder.
Red asphalt means bike lane: never walk in it, and look both ways for bikes before stepping off any curb.
The free ferries behind Centraal Station are a mini harbor cruise in themselves and take you to the bars and galleries of Amsterdam-Noord.
If you plan to visit three or more museums, compare the cost of a Museumkaart, a pass covering dozens of museums across the Netherlands.
Rent a bike with hand brakes if you're not used to Dutch back-pedal brakes, and always lock both the frame and a wheel to something solid.
etiquette: Never photograph the windows in the red-light district; it's disrespectful to the workers and can provoke a sharp reaction.
Dutch directness isn't rudeness, so expect honest opinions and feel free to give them back.
Splitting the bill, known the world over as 'going Dutch', is completely normal, even on a date.
Smoking cannabis on the street in the old center is banned, and drinking alcohol outdoors there can also bring a fine.

neighborhoods.name: Jordaan
neighborhoods.blurb: Narrow canals, flower-draped façades, hidden almshouse courtyards and cozy brown cafés.

neighborhoods.name: Canal Ring
neighborhoods.blurb: The UNESCO-listed crescent of Golden Age canals and merchants' mansions, including the boutique-filled Nine Streets.

neighborhoods.name: De Pijp
neighborhoods.blurb: A lively, multicultural district of markets, global eateries and terrace bars around the Albert Cuyp Market.

neighborhoods.name: Amsterdam-Noord
neighborhoods.blurb: A creative, post-industrial zone across the IJ, with shipyards turned art spaces, a lookout tower and waterside cafés.

neighborhoods.name: Oud-West
neighborhoods.blurb: Leafy and residential around the Vondelpark, with a food hall in a former tram depot and relaxed neighborhood bars.

dishes.name: Bitterballen
dishes.description: Crisp breadcrumbed spheres of molten beef ragout served with mustard, the classic bar snack; let them cool a moment before biting.

dishes.name: Hollandse Nieuwe
dishes.description: Lightly brined young herring of the new season, eaten raw with onions and pickles or held by the tail and lowered into your mouth.

dishes.name: Stroopwafel
dishes.description: Two thin waffle wafers sandwiching gooey caramel syrup; buy them hot off the iron at a market for the full effect.

dishes.name: Appeltaart
dishes.description: Deep-dish Dutch apple pie packed with cinnamon-spiced apples under a lattice crust, served with a generous cloud of whipped cream.

dishes.name: Jenever
dishes.description: The juniper-scented grain spirit that inspired gin, sipped from a tulip-shaped glass in centuries-old tasting rooms.

events.name: King's Day
events.description: On April 27 the whole city turns orange for a giant street party, with a citywide flea market, packed party boats and concerts.

events.name: Pride Amsterdam
events.description: The highlight is the Canal Parade, when dozens of extravagantly decorated boats cruise the Prinsengracht past cheering crowds.

events.name: Amsterdam Dance Event
events.description: The world's biggest club festival and electronic music conference takes over hundreds of venues for five nonstop days.

events.name: Amsterdam Light Festival
events.description: From late November into January, artists' light installations illuminate the canals, best seen from an evening boat.

attractions.name: Rijksmuseum
attractions.description: The Netherlands' treasure house is a cathedral-like palace of Golden Age art, crowned by Rembrandt's monumental Night Watch in the Gallery of Honour. Beyond the Vermeers, seek out the intricate 17th-century dollhouses and the spiral-staircased library, then watch cyclists sweep through the passage beneath the building.
attractions.bookingTip: Book a timed ticket online and head straight to the Gallery of Honour at opening, before the tour groups arrive.

attractions.name: Van Gogh Museum
attractions.description: The world's largest collection of Van Gogh's work traces his short, turbulent career from somber Dutch peasant scenes to the blazing sunflowers and almond blossoms of his final years in France. Letters to his brother Theo, displayed alongside the paintings, make the story all the more poignant.
attractions.bookingTip: Tickets are sold only online in timed slots and often sell out several days ahead in summer.

attractions.name: Anne Frank House
attractions.description: The canal house where Anne Frank and seven others hid from Nazi persecution for more than two years is preserved with devastating simplicity, from the swinging bookcase to pencil marks recording the girls' heights. It's a quiet, profoundly moving visit that stays with you long after you leave.
attractions.bookingTip: Tickets are sold only online, released six weeks in advance, and usually disappear within hours.

attractions.name: Vondelpark
attractions.description: Amsterdam's favorite back garden is a sweep of lawns, ponds and winding paths where locals picnic, jog and cycle from dawn till dusk. Summer brings free performances at the open-air theater, and the rose garden and lakeside café make pleasant pit stops.
attractions.bookingTip: No tickets needed; check the open-air theater's summer program for free weekend concerts and dance shows.

attractions.name: Jordaan
attractions.description: Once a working-class district of artisans and immigrants, the Jordaan is now the city's most charming neighborhood, a grid of narrow canals, flower boxes, hidden almshouse courtyards and snug brown cafés. Browse the Nine Streets' boutiques on its edge and time your visit for the Saturday farmers' market by the Noorderkerk.
attractions.hours: Always open; Noordermarkt on Monday and Saturday mornings
attractions.bookingTip: Free to explore; some courtyard almshouses welcome quiet visitors on weekday daytimes but close their doors at weekends.

attractions.name: Albert Cuyp Market
attractions.description: The Netherlands' best-known street market runs for several blocks through De Pijp, with hundreds of stalls selling everything from Gouda wheels and fresh herring to fabric and phone cases. Snack as you go on stroopwafels pressed to order and poffertjes dusted with powdered sugar.
attractions.bookingTip: Visit on a weekday morning for the calmest browsing, and carry a little cash for the few stalls that still prefer it.

attractions.name: Eye Filmmuseum
attractions.description: A gleaming white, angular building that looks poised for take-off on the IJ waterfront, the Eye houses the national film archive, four cinemas and changing exhibitions on filmmakers and moving-image artists. A free basement space lets you dip into clips from a century of cinema, and the waterside café terrace looks straight back across the river to Centraal Station.
attractions.hours: 10:00–19:00 daily for exhibitions; screenings until late
attractions.bookingTip: Ride the free ferry from behind Centraal Station, which docks right beside the building, and book exhibition tickets online to save a little.

attractions.name: Royal Palace of Amsterdam
attractions.description: Built as the city hall at the height of the Golden Age, this vast classical palace on Dam Square was designed to show the world Amsterdam's wealth. Inside, the marble Citizens' Hall has maps of the heavens and the earth inlaid into its floor, and the royal family still uses the building for state occasions.
attractions.bookingTip: Check the website before visiting, as the palace closes for state visits and receptions; the included audio guide is excellent.

attractions.name: Oude Kerk
attractions.description: Amsterdam's oldest building, a 14th-century Gothic church with a glorious timber-vaulted roof, stands startlingly in the middle of the red-light district. Today it doubles as a contemporary art venue, and Rembrandt's wife Saskia lies buried beneath its worn floor stones.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy tickets at the door, and in summer look out for guided tower climbs with a rare view over the old city's rooftops.

attractions.name: Begijnhof
attractions.description: Push through an unassuming door off the Spui and you step into a hushed courtyard of tall almshouses around a lawn, home to communities of religious women since the Middle Ages. Look for the black timber house front at number 34, one of only two wooden façades left in the city.
attractions.bookingTip: Entry is free, but residents still live here, so visit in small groups and keep your voice low.

hotels.name: Het Zilverhuis aan de Herengracht
hotels.description: Three joined 17th-century merchants' houses on the grandest stretch of the Herengracht, restored with silk wallpapers, Delft-tile fireplaces and a hidden garden running back from the canal. A candlelit spa fills the vaulted basement, and a private launch takes guests on canal cruises.

hotels.name: Pakhuis Lindengracht
hotels.description: A converted spice warehouse on a Jordaan canal, with steep original staircases, chunky timber beams and rooms dressed in Dutch design pieces. The ground-floor café bakes superb apple cake, and bikes are included in the rate.

hotels.name: Fietsbel Hostel
hotels.description: A cheerful hostel in a former schoolhouse on the edge of the Vondelpark, with bright dorms, a garden terrace and a bar where travelers swap route tips. Rent a bike downstairs and you're pedaling through the park in thirty seconds.

hotels.name: Hotel Veerpont Noord
hotels.description: Industrial chic on the north bank of the IJ, with raw concrete, recycled ship steel and floor-to-ceiling windows framing the passing ferries. The rooftop sauna and hot tub are the perfect end to a day of exploring.

hotels.name: Villa Esdoorn
hotels.description: A stately 1890s villa in the Museum Quarter, with stained-glass stairwells, marble fireplaces and a lush garden shaded by an old maple tree. The Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum are both a five-minute walk away.

hotels.name: Steenhouwer Apartments
hotels.description: Bright, Scandinavian-style apartments above a former stonemason's workshop in De Pijp, each with a full kitchen for cooking your market finds. The neighborhood's bars and cafés are right outside the door.

restaurants.name: Zeegras
restaurants.description: A canal-side dining room of pale wood and sea-green velvet, where tasting menus celebrate the North Sea, the polders and foraged Dutch herbs. Expect Zeeland oysters, smoked eel and a thoughtful list of Dutch and German wines.

restaurants.name: Café De Scheve Balk
restaurants.description: A classic brown café whose walls were stained amber by generations of pipe smoke and conversation, with a crooked ceiling beam that gives the place its name. Order a local beer and a plate of crisp bitterballen with mustard, then settle in.

restaurants.name: Ochtendgloren
restaurants.description: A light-flooded corner café by the Vondelpark gates, loved for fluffy Dutch pancakes, excellent flat whites and granola with local yogurt. Laptop workers claim the long table on weekdays, while weekends bring a queue for brunch.
restaurants.signatureDish: Dutch pancake with apple and cinnamon

restaurants.name: De Zilte Kar
restaurants.description: A green-painted fish cart where herring is filleted to order and served with chopped onions and pickles or tucked into a soft bun. It's also the spot to try kibbeling, crisp battered cod bites with garlic sauce.
restaurants.signatureDish: Hollandse Nieuwe herring on a bun

restaurants.name: Rumah Kenari
restaurants.description: Brass lanterns and batik textiles set the scene for an epic rijsttafel, the Dutch-Indonesian feast of fifteen or more small dishes. Beef rendang, satay with peanut sauce and sambal-fried green beans crowd every inch of the table.

restaurants.name: Roti Mi Kondre
restaurants.description: A tiny, perpetually busy takeaway serving Surinamese roti wraps stuffed with curried chicken, long beans and potato, plus sandwiches of slow-cooked pork. Eat on the waterfront benches with a view of the ferries.

restaurants.name: Pannenkoekenhuis Het Karnemelkje
restaurants.description: Plate-sized Dutch pancakes, sweet or savory, fill the menu at this cozy house of Delft tiles and a crackling stove. Try the classic bacon and apple drizzled with stroop syrup, and let the kids choose from a whole page of toppings.
restaurants.signatureDish: Bacon and apple pancake with stroop

restaurants.name: Proeflokaal De Kandelaar
restaurants.description: A creaky old tasting room where jenever is poured to the brim, so tradition dictates you bend down and take the first sip without lifting the glass. Snack on aged Gouda and smoked sausage while choosing from dozens of Dutch gins and liqueurs.

experiences.name: Stille Sloep Twilight Canal Cruise
experiences.description: Glide through the canal ring aboard a silent electric sloop at dusk, just as the bridges light up and the gabled houses glow. Your born-and-raised skipper shares houseboat gossip and hidden-gable stories while you sip Dutch wine over a cheese platter.

experiences.name: Waterland Windmills and Cheese Farm Bike Ride
experiences.description: Hop the ferry to Noord and pedal quiet dike roads into the polders of Waterland, past grazing cows, wooden villages and windmills. At a family farm you'll taste Gouda made on site and try on a pair of wooden clogs.

experiences.name: De Pijp Market Bites Walk
experiences.description: Taste your way through the Albert Cuyp Market and the multicultural streets of De Pijp, from fresh herring and warm stroopwafels to Surinamese roti and Turkish pastries. The walk winds up in a brown café with a flight of local craft beer.

experiences.name: Golden Age Light: Oil Painting Workshop
experiences.description: Start with a short gallery talk on how the Dutch masters handled light, then retreat to a canal-side studio to paint your own still life in oils. A professional artist guides every step, and your canvas is wrapped to take home.
